question: What are the canonical names and definitions for the parts of Linux epoll that edge-triggered mode (EPOLLET) touches? Find the terms the man pages and the kernel use, each with its definition: epoll instance, interest list, ready list, edge-triggered vs level-triggered, EPOLLET, EPOLLONESHOT, EPOLLEXCLUSIVE, EPOLLRDHUP, EPOLLIN/EPOLLOUT, EAGAIN/EWOULDBLOCK, "open file description" vs file descriptor, and the kernel's own names where they differ (eventpoll, epitem, the wakeup callback). Use Rank 1 or Rank 3 sources only for the definitions.

sources.rank_basis: tier A: github.com/torvalds/linux/ (source at release tag v6.12)
tier B: class (spec: POSIX.1-2024, The Open Group Base Specifications Issue 8, XBD Definitions)

facts.summary: epoll(7) names the central object the epoll instance: an in-kernel data structure that user space can treat as a container of two lists.
facts.quote: The central concept of the epoll API is the epoll instance, an in- kernel data structure which, from a user-space perspective, can be considered as a container for two lists

facts.summary: The interest list (also called the epoll set) is the set of file descriptors the process registered to monitor.
facts.quote: The interest list (sometimes also called the epoll set): the set of file descriptors that the process has registered an interest in monitoring.

facts.summary: The ready list is the set of descriptors ready for I/O, a set of references into the interest list, filled by the kernel as I/O happens.
facts.quote: The ready list: the set of file descriptors that are "ready" for I/O. The ready list is a subset of (or, more precisely, a set of references to) the file descriptors in the interest list. The ready list is dynamically populated by the kernel as a result of I/O activity on those file descriptors.

facts.summary: epoll_create(2) creates an instance and returns a file descriptor to it; epoll_ctl(2) adds items to the interest list; epoll_wait(2) blocks until events and can be seen as fetching from the ready list.
facts.quote: epoll_create(2) creates a new epoll instance and returns a file descriptor referring to that instance. … Interest in particular file descriptors is then registered via epoll_ctl(2), which adds items to the interest list of the epoll instance. … epoll_wait(2) waits for I/O events, blocking the calling thread if no events are currently available. (This system call can be thought of as fetching items from the ready list of the epoll instance.)

facts.summary: The man page names the two modes edge-triggered (ET) and level-triggered (LT).
facts.quote: The epoll event distribution interface is able to behave both as edge-triggered (ET) and as level-triggered (LT).

facts.summary: Edge-triggered mode delivers events only when the monitored descriptor changes, i.e. one event per received chunk of data.
facts.quote: The reason for this is that edge-triggered mode delivers events only when changes occur on the monitored file descriptor, that is, an event will be generated upon each receipt of a chunk of data.

facts.summary: An EPOLLET user should use nonblocking descriptors, and the suggested use is to wait for an event only after read(2) or write(2) returns EAGAIN.
facts.quote: An application that employs the EPOLLET flag should use nonblocking file descriptors to avoid having a blocking read or write starve a task that is handling multiple file descriptors. The suggested way to use epoll as an edge-triggered (EPOLLET) interface is as follows: (1) with nonblocking file descriptors; and (2) by waiting for an event only after read(2) or write(2) return EAGAIN.

facts.summary: Level-triggered is the default (EPOLLET not given); in that mode epoll has the same semantics as poll(2), only faster.
facts.quote: By contrast, when used as a level-triggered interface (the default, when EPOLLET is not specified), epoll is simply a faster poll(2), and can be used wherever the latter is used since it shares the same semantics.

facts.summary: Because ET can still give several events for several chunks, EPOLLONESHOT disables the descriptor after one event; the caller must rearm it with EPOLL_CTL_MOD.
facts.quote: Since even with edge-triggered epoll, multiple events can be generated upon receipt of multiple chunks of data, the caller has the option to specify the EPOLLONESHOT flag, to tell epoll to disable the associated file descriptor after the receipt of an event with epoll_wait(2). When the EPOLLONESHOT flag is specified, it is the caller's responsibility to rearm the file descriptor using epoll_ctl(2) with EPOLL_CTL_MOD.

facts.summary: When several threads or processes block in epoll_wait(2) on the same epoll file descriptor and an EPOLLET-marked descriptor becomes ready, only one of them is woken; the page calls this avoiding thundering herd wake-ups.
facts.quote: If multiple threads (or processes, if child processes have inherited the epoll file descriptor across fork(2)) are blocked in epoll_wait(2) waiting on the same epoll file descriptor and a file descriptor in the interest list that is marked for edge-triggered (EPOLLET) notification becomes ready, just one of the threads (or processes) is awoken from epoll_wait(2).

facts.summary: An interest-list entry is keyed by the file descriptor number together with the open file description, which the page also calls an open file handle, the kernel's internal representation of an open file.
facts.quote: The key is the combination of the file descriptor number and the open file description (also known as an "open file handle", the kernel's internal representation of an open file).

facts.summary: A file descriptor is a reference to an open file description; dup(2), dup2(2), fcntl(2) F_DUPFD and fork(2) create new descriptors to the same description, which lives until all of them are closed.
facts.quote: A file descriptor is a reference to an open file description (see open(2)). Whenever a file descriptor is duplicated via dup(2), dup2(2), fcntl(2) F_DUPFD, or fork(2), a new file descriptor referring to the same open file description is created. An open file description continues to exist until all file descriptors referring to it have been closed.

facts.summary: epoll_ctl() adds, modifies or removes entries in the interest list of the epoll instance named by epfd.
facts.quote: This system call is used to add, modify, or remove entries in the interest list of the epoll(7) instance referred to by the file descriptor epfd.

facts.summary: An EPOLL_CTL_ADD entry holds the file descriptor, a reference to its open file description, and the settings from event.
facts.quote: EPOLL_CTL_ADD Add an entry to the interest list of the epoll file descriptor, epfd. The entry includes the file descriptor, fd, a reference to the corresponding open file description (see epoll(7) and open(2)), and the settings specified in event.

facts.summary: The events mask mixes two kinds of bits: event types, which epoll_wait(2) returns, and input flags, which change behaviour but are not returned.
facts.quote: The events member of the epoll_event structure is a bit mask composed by ORing together zero or more event types, returned by epoll_wait(2), and input flags, which affect its behavior, but aren't returned.

facts.summary: EPOLLIN means the file is available for read(2); EPOLLOUT means it is available for write(2).
facts.quote: EPOLLIN The associated file is available for read(2) operations. EPOLLOUT The associated file is available for write(2) operations.

facts.summary: EPOLLRDHUP (since Linux 2.6.17) reports that a stream socket peer closed or shut down its writing half; the page says it helps detect peer shutdown under edge-triggered monitoring.
facts.quote: EPOLLRDHUP (since Linux 2.6.17) Stream socket peer closed connection, or shut down writing half of connection. (This flag is especially useful for writing simple code to detect peer shutdown when using edge-triggered monitoring.)

facts.summary: EPOLLHUP is a hang-up on the descriptor; epoll_wait(2) always waits for it, so it need not be set in events.
facts.quote: EPOLLHUP Hang up happened on the associated file descriptor. epoll_wait(2) will always wait for this event; it is not necessary to set it in events when calling epoll_ctl().

facts.summary: EPOLLET is an input flag that requests edge-triggered notification; epoll's default is level-triggered.
facts.quote: EPOLLET Requests edge-triggered notification for the associated file descriptor. The default behavior for epoll is level- triggered.

facts.summary: EPOLLONESHOT (since Linux 2.6.2): after one event the descriptor is disabled in the interest list; the user must call epoll_ctl() with EPOLL_CTL_MOD to rearm it with a new mask.
facts.quote: EPOLLONESHOT (since Linux 2.6.2) Requests one-shot notification for the associated file descriptor. This means that after an event notified for the file descriptor by epoll_wait(2), the file descriptor is disabled in the interest list and no other events will be reported by the epoll interface. The user must call epoll_ctl() with EPOLL_CTL_MOD to rearm the file descriptor with a new event mask.

facts.summary: EPOLLWAKEUP (since Linux 3.5) keeps the system from suspending while the event is pending or processed, under the stated conditions that EPOLLONESHOT and EPOLLET are clear and the process has CAP_BLOCK_SUSPEND.
facts.quote: EPOLLWAKEUP (since Linux 3.5) If EPOLLONESHOT and EPOLLET are clear and the process has the CAP_BLOCK_SUSPEND capability, ensure that the system does not enter "suspend" or "hibernate" while this event is pending or being processed.

facts.summary: EPOLLEXCLUSIVE (since Linux 4.5) sets an exclusive wakeup mode: when several epoll file descriptors attach to the same target with it, one or more of them get the event, instead of all of them by default.
facts.quote: EPOLLEXCLUSIVE (since Linux 4.5) Sets an exclusive wakeup mode for the epoll file descriptor that is being attached to the target file descriptor, fd. When a wakeup event occurs and multiple epoll file descriptors are attached to the same target file using EPOLLEXCLUSIVE, one or more of the epoll file descriptors will receive an event with epoll_wait(2). The default in this scenario (when EPOLLEXCLUSIVE is not set) is for all epoll file descriptors to receive an event.

facts.summary: With EPOLLEXCLUSIVE only EPOLLIN, EPOLLOUT, EPOLLWAKEUP and EPOLLET (plus optional EPOLLHUP, EPOLLERR) may be given; any other value fails with EINVAL.
facts.quote: The following values may be specified in conjunction with EPOLLEXCLUSIVE: EPOLLIN, EPOLLOUT, EPOLLWAKEUP, and EPOLLET. EPOLLHUP and EPOLLERR can also be specified, but this is not required … Attempts to specify other values in events yield the error EINVAL.

facts.summary: EPOLLEXCLUSIVE is accepted only with EPOLL_CTL_ADD; using it with EPOLL_CTL_MOD, a later MOD on the same pair, or a target that is an epoll instance all fail with EINVAL.
facts.quote: EPOLLEXCLUSIVE may be used only in an EPOLL_CTL_ADD operation; attempts to employ it with EPOLL_CTL_MOD yield an error. … The error in all of these cases is EINVAL.

facts.summary: In the kernel, the epoll instance is struct eventpoll, kept in the private_data member of the epoll file's struct file and described as the main data structure of the eventpoll interface.
facts.quote: This structure is stored inside the "private_data" member of the file … structure and represents the main data structure for the eventpoll

facts.summary: struct eventpoll holds the ready list as rdllist (a list of ready file descriptors) and the monitored descriptors in an RB tree rooted at rbr.
facts.quote: /* List of ready file descriptors */ … struct list_head rdllist; … /* RB tree root used to store monitored fd structs */ … struct rb_root_cached rbr;

facts.summary: struct eventpoll also has ovflist, a singly linked chain of epitems that became ready while events were being copied to user space without holding the lock.
facts.quote: This is a single linked list that chains all the "struct epitem" that … happened while transferring ready events to userspace w/out … holding ->lock. … struct epitem *ovflist;

facts.summary: Each descriptor added to epoll gets a struct epitem linked into the rbr RB tree; its rdllink field links it into the eventpoll ready list.
facts.quote: Each file descriptor added to the eventpoll interface will … have an entry of this type linked to the "rbr" RB tree. … struct epitem { … /* List header used to link this structure to the eventpoll ready list */ … struct list_head rdllink;

facts.summary: ep_cmp_ffd compares RB tree keys by the struct file pointer first and by the fd number second.
facts.quote: /* Compare RB tree keys */ … static inline int ep_cmp_ffd(struct epoll_filefd *p1, … return (p1->file > p2->file ? +1: … (p1->file < p2->file ? -1 : p1->fd - p2->fd));

facts.summary: The wakeup callback is ep_poll_callback: the function given to the wait-queue wakeup mechanism, called by the watched files when they have events.
facts.quote: This is the callback that is passed to the wait queue wakeup … mechanism. It is called by the stored file descriptors when they … have events to report.

facts.summary: ep_poll_callback chains the epitem on ovflist while events are being copied to user space, and otherwise adds it to the tail of rdllist (the ready list).
facts.quote: If we are transferring events to userspace, we can hold no locks … All the events that happen during that period of time are … chained in ep->ovflist and requeued later on. … /* In the usual case, add event to ready list. */ … if (list_add_tail_lockless(&epi->rdllink, &ep->rdllist))

loc.heading: static int ep_poll_callback(wait_queue_entry_t *wait, unsigned mode, int sync, void *key)

facts.summary: ep_poll_callback treats an item whose mask has no poll(2) event bits as disabled, which the comment ties to EPOLLONESHOT until the next EPOLL_CTL_MOD.
facts.quote: If the event mask does not contain any poll(2) event, we consider the … descriptor to be disabled. This condition is likely the effect of the … EPOLLONESHOT bit that disables the descriptor when an event is received, … until the next EPOLL_CTL_MOD will be issued.

loc.heading: static int ep_poll_callback(wait_queue_entry_t *wait, unsigned mode, int sync, void *key)

facts.summary: The kernel groups EPOLLWAKEUP, EPOLLONESHOT, EPOLLET and EPOLLEXCLUSIVE as EP_PRIVATE_BITS, the epoll private bits of the event mask.
facts.quote: /* Epoll private bits inside the event mask */ … #define EP_PRIVATE_BITS (EPOLLWAKEUP | EPOLLONESHOT | EPOLLET | EPOLLEXCLUSIVE)

facts.summary: In ep_send_events, after an event is delivered, an EPOLLONESHOT item has its mask cut to the private bits; an item without EPOLLET (level-triggered) is put back on the ready list so the next epoll_wait() checks it again.
facts.quote: if (epi->event.events & EPOLLONESHOT) … epi->event.events &= EP_PRIVATE_BITS; … else if (!(epi->event.events & EPOLLET)) { … If this file has been added with Level … Trigger mode, we need to insert back inside … the ready list, so that the next call to … epoll_wait() will check again the events

facts.summary: ep_ptable_queue_proc installs ep_poll_callback as the wait-queue entry function on the target file, queued with add_wait_queue_exclusive when EPOLLEXCLUSIVE is set and add_wait_queue otherwise.
facts.quote: init_waitqueue_func_entry(&pwq->wait, ep_poll_callback); … if (epi->event.events & EPOLLEXCLUSIVE) … add_wait_queue_exclusive(whead, &pwq->wait); … add_wait_queue(whead, &pwq->wait);

facts.summary: In ep_poll (the epoll_wait path), when no events are available the calling task is added to the instance wait queue ep->wq as an exclusive waiter; this code path has no EPOLLET test.
facts.quote: eavail = ep_events_available(ep); … if (!eavail) … __add_wait_queue_exclusive(&ep->wq, &wait);

loc.heading: static int ep_poll(struct eventpoll *ep, struct epoll_event __user *events,

facts.summary: ep_done_scan splices leftover items back onto rdllist and, if the ready list is not empty, wakes ep->wq again.
facts.quote: Quickly re-inject items left on "txlist". … list_splice(txlist, &ep->rdllist); … if (!list_empty(&ep->rdllist)) { … if (waitqueue_active(&ep->wq)) … wake_up(&ep->wq);

facts.summary: POSIX defines an open file description as a record of how processes access a file; each file descriptor refers to exactly one, one description can have several descriptors, and offset, status and access modes belong to the description.
facts.quote: A record of how a process or group of processes is accessing a file. Each file descriptor refers to exactly one open file description, but an open file description can be referred to by more than one file descriptor. The file offset, file status, and file access modes are attributes of an open file description.

facts.summary: POSIX defines a file descriptor as a per-process unique, non-negative integer that identifies an open file for file access.
facts.quote: A per-process unique, non-negative integer used to identify an open file for the purpose of file access.

facts.summary: POSIX defines an open file as a file currently associated with a file descriptor.
facts.quote: A file that is currently associated with a file descriptor.

facts.summary: POSIX treats "file description" as another name that points to the Open File Description entry.
facts.quote: See Open File Description in 3.241 Open File Description.

facts.summary: POSIX defines non-blocking as a property of an open file description that makes calls return without delay when the action cannot finish without unknown delay; for reads from ttys and FIFOs the read returns at once when no data is available.
facts.quote: A property of an open file description that causes function calls involving it to return without delay when it is detected that the requested action associated with the function call cannot be completed without unknown delay. … For data reads from devices … such as ttys and FIFOs, this property causes the read to return immediately when no data was available.

facts.summary: POSIX defines blocking as a property of an open file description that makes calls wait for the requested action before returning.
facts.quote: A property of an open file description that causes function calls associated with it to wait for the requested action to be performed before returning.

conflicts.topic: is the single-waiter wakeup specific to EPOLLET?
conflicts.note: epoll(7) ties waking just one epoll_wait() thread to EPOLLET-marked descriptors; the v6.12 source queues every sleeper exclusively without an EPOLLET test and re-wakes ep->wq when items stay on rdllist (level-triggered re-insert)
